record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Can the causal-set nonlocal d'Alembertian field theories used for off-shell dark matter be extended beyond scalar fields to other kinds of fields, so that the framework is not limited to scalar-field propagation and scalar-field phenomenology?

evidence.quote: Nonlocal analogues of the d’Alembertian operator □ that describe the propagation of scalar fields, exist more commonly in causal set theory than their more conventional local counterparts.
Our discussion will be limited to scalar field theories. The extension to other kinds of fields is not presently known.

artifact.status_search_result: Literature searches reveal that nonlocal causal-set d'Alembertians are well-developed for scalar fields and have been generalized within the scalar sector (e.g., generalized families in arbitrary dimension). Some preliminary work exists on free fermions on causal sets and on retarded Green-function approaches for spin-half particles, but a fully developed extension of the nonlocal d'Alembertian framework to vector, spinor, or higher-tensor fields, satisfying the same Lorentz-invariance and continuum-limit guarantees, has not been established. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Generalized causal set d'Alembertians
status_evidence.snippet: A family of generalized d'Alembertian operators in D-dimensional Minkowski spacetimes ... The prototypes of these operators arose as averages of matrix operators meant to describe the propagation of a scalar field in a causal set.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations exist primarily within the scalar-field setting.

status_evidence.title: Free Fermions on causal sets
status_evidence.snippet: Models for continuum-based phenomenology and spin-half particles on a causal set.
status_evidence.claim: Preliminary fermion constructions exist but do not directly extend the nonlocal d'Alembertian framework.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Field Theory On Causal Sets
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlocality of causal set theory causes problems in defining differential operators within the causal set framework.
status_evidence.claim: General field-theoretic differential operators beyond scalars remain problematic.
